To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the overall reactivities of organohalides toward granular zerovalent iron, Cr(2+) and an iron porphyrin can be predicted from their reactivities toward Cr(2+), but not from their reactivities towards an iron porphirin.

(1) The reactivity of organohalides toward Cr(2+) is correlated by the Hammett equation, with a slope of -1.1, and (2) the reactivity of organochlorides toward granu-lar iron is correlated by the Taft equation, with a steric term of 1.0, and a polar term of 0.9.

cross-correlation plots between the rate constants for the reduction of benzotrichloroide by three different reductants (Fe(II)TCP, granular iron, and Cr(II)) show good linear correlation, but the slopes are not equal to one.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reduction of organic compounds by granular iron and the use of correlations to study the mechanisms of these reactions.
the reactivity of substituted benzotrifluorides, benzotrifluoroacetates, benzotrichlrorides and substituted benzotriflates toward granular iron.
the development of a new method for the determination of the reactivity of organic pollutants with iron(II), iron(III), chromium(III), and chromium(II).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a correlation analysis is a valuable tool for predicting the reactivity of organic pollutants, but not for deducing their mechanisms of reduction.
a slope of 1 is a necessary but insufficient condition for the existence of a common mechanistic pathway.
cross-correlations are useful, but that they should be interpreted with caution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the rate constants for the reaction between benzotrichloroide and the three reductants studied are all sensitive to steric effects and that, in the case of the iron reductants, there is no evidence for the existence of a common mechanism.

benzotrichloroide is reduced by Cr(H2O)(6)(2+) and Fe(II) porphyin via a dissociative inner sphere mechanism, and that benzotrichoride and its substituted analogs are reduced by granular iron via a mechanism that may be different from that of Cr(H2O))(6)(2+), and may involve an inner sphere mechanism, a surface mechanism, or a combination of both.
the more reactive the reductant, the faster the reaction with benzotrichloridate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cross-correlations of rate data should be interpreted with care.
the use of cross-correlation plots to support mechanistic hypotheses must be done with caution.
the reactivity of organohalides toward granular Fe is not well understood and requires further study.
